## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. - unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.

- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

The repo had **no** local packs; this adds its first.

## The gap

Manifesting the stack turned up one genuinely unhomed, non-vestigial concern: the comment **CATEGORY taxonomy**. `shared/categories.mjs` is a single source both halves read (server write-time allowlist + read-time default; the extension's picker, filter bar, badges and per-category look), but its *presentation layer* lives in four files nothing links back to it — `extension/src/categories//design.mjs`, the sibling scoped `.css`, the `registry.mjs` `DESIGNS` map, and the `sidepanel.html` stylesheet links. Every one of them **fails silently**: `designFor()` falls back to the default category's descriptor, an unlinked stylesheet simply never applies. Append a category without them and it ships wearing another category's copy and colours, with no test, build or runtime error.

No canon pack homes this (it's the product itself, so it belongs in a local pack by design), and no existing local pack owns the territory.

## The pack — `.claudinite/local/packs/tldr-categories/`

Checks-first, per the promotion ladder:

| Rung | Rule |
|---|---|
| check (blocking) | `tldr-categories/presentation-lockstep` — every id in `CATEGORIES` has its `design.mjs` (with matching `id`), its `body[data-category=""]`-scoped css, its registry import **and** `DESIGNS` entry, and its `sidepanel.html` link; `DEFAULT_CATEGORY` is a real id |
| check (blocking) | `tldr-categories/ids-append-only` — a shipped id (persisted on every comment, half the `#` `CategoryRankIndex` key) is never renamed, removed or reordered; appending needs no edit to the check |
| prose (`RULES.md`) | ids are stored data / labels aren't; unknown + absent categories degrade rather than error; the GSI has no backfill; categories differ in look, never in behaviour |

Both rules are `scope: 'world'` and dependency-free (plain finding objects, no engine import), so they run without the gitignored mount.

## The CI check — red-first

`pack.test.mjs` asserts each rule **fires** on a violating in-memory fixture (missing folder → all five findings; import-without-`DESIGNS`-entry; unscoped css; unlinked stylesheet; mismatched descriptor id; bogus `DEFAULT_CATEGORY`; renamed/removed/prepended id), **is silent** on a clean one, and that the **real repo passes today**. Verified against the real tree too: overlaying a 4th category on `shared/categories.mjs` produces exactly the five expected blocking findings.

Wired into the root `npm test` and the `test: extension` workflow's path filters (it guards `shared/categories.mjs` + `extension/src/categories/`, already in that workflow's scope). Declared as `tldr-categories` in `.claudinite-checks.json`; `check_the_world` loads it clean — the only blocking findings are the two pre-existing `claudinite-isolation` ones on `CLAUDE.md` / `dev/procedures/working-instructions.md`.

## Note, not acted on

`server/` is a substantial AWS SAM app and `dev/procedures/aws-sam.md` states the portable subsets already live in a **canon `aws-sam` pack** — but `.claudinite-checks.json` never declares it (which is why it isn't in the vendored shelf). The right action is to **declare canon `aws-sam`** once the mount carries it, not to re-create it locally; logged on the tracker rather than done here, since declaring an id the mount doesn't know is a settings error.

Two canon packs are matched by this repo's real files (both are *fingerprinted* packs — the fingerprint only suspects, declaring is still the project's call) and are declared nowhere in `.claudinite-checks.json`, so neither is vendored into `.claudinite/shared/packs/` and neither contributes prose, checks or skills to any session:

| Pack | Fingerprint (per `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`) | This repo's matching evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `aws-sam` | a SAM template (`template.yaml`/`.yml`) | `server/template.yaml` (`Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31`), `server/samconfig.toml`, `sam build` / `sam validate --lint` in `server/package.json`, `aws-actions/setup-sam@v3` in `deploy.yml` and `test-server.yml`, the `Metadata.BuildMethod: esbuild` bundling block |

What is unhomed is the **server-side validation** half: audience pinning, issuer, `email_verified`.

## What breaks while this is off

- Rules for the SAM/Lambda/API-Gateway/DynamoDB layer and for server-side ID-token validation never load, so every session touching `server/` re-derives them or misses them. ## Do not fix it by editing the declaration list

The declaration and the re-vendor have to land together, which is what the `adopt-pack` skill does (declare → adoption interview → re-vendor → scaffold).

- [ ] Run `adopt-pack` for `google-identity`.

That is the `growth-dedup` skill's job, not this one's.

## Closing condition

Both packs are declared in `.claudinite-checks.json`, both are vendored in the mount, and `check_the_world.mjs` is green. # Executable requirements — the TLDR extension (UI + server)

This folder is a self-contained methodology for **executable requirements**: a way to drive
development where every requirement is backed by a test that proves it, the suite fails the moment a
requirement is added without a proof, and the *expected* result of each proof is owned by the project
owner — never silently changed by an agent to make a red build go green. It is **cross-tier**: a
product requirement is stated once, with its client-UI proof and (where the real boundary is the
backend) its server proof as sibling leaves.

The shape here — a numbered spec, a strict leaf⇄case bijection, kinds as a pluggable contract,
owner-owned expecteds, snapshots driven through the real code — is the reusable pattern. It is
adapted from [`missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator` `dev/requirements/`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/tree/main/dev/requirements);
the portable, project-agnostic write-up of *why* and *how* lives in
[`dev/docs/ui-testing-guideline.md`](../docs/ui-testing-guideline.md).

   [`requirements-coverage.test.mjs`](requirements-coverage.test.mjs) — which also checks that every
   discovered kind has a runner that *executes* its cases (a claimed-but-never-run leaf fails), and
   that the set of skipped `tbd` leaves matches a committed allowlist (so a wired leaf can't be
   silently downgraded to unverified).
3. **Kinds are extensible.** A *kind* is one way a requirement can be asserted (a rendered-state
